_comment: Tooling-setup corpus. Positives are examiner intents about a repository's toolchain configuration — what is declared, whether CI runs it, what to pin, which of two equivalent tools to keep. Negatives are the three boundaries this skill states for itself and one it inherits. First, running the tools or fixing what they report is a coding concern, not a setup one ('run ruff over the codebase', 'fix the type errors mypy is reporting'). Second, installing is outside the consent model entirely. Third, markdown formatting has its own home, which is the sharpest boundary here because the sibling corpus is full of lint-and-format vocabulary — the discriminator is the subject, repo tooling versus prose. The fourth is repo health: legal, community, and branch-protection conventions are a different audit that also says 'what is this repo missing'. One negative is deliberately adversarial rather than distant: 'summarize why this CI job failed' sits inside this skill's own vocabulary — it reads CI to establish whether tools run — and still belongs elsewhere, because interpreting a failure is change-narration work while establishing whether anything runs at all is this one's.
